Product PRD & Overview: Unified Inference (v9) - 2026-12-01

Summary
-------
This document describes the vision, product requirements, design considerations, roadmap themes, pricing/packaging guidance, and release notes for Unified Inference v9 — Redwood Inference's next major product milestone focused on developer ergonomics, cost-aware routing, and improved private deployment UX. v9 consolidates prior Optimize features, expands Dedicated/reserved capacity controls, and introduces a simpler tiered packaging model for enterprise customers.

Goals and success metrics
-------------------------
- Make it trivial for engineering teams to: pin a model version, configure cost-and-latency routing policies, and apply safe rollouts across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Reduce per-token cost by 15% on typical web-chat workloads via smarter default batching and cache profiles within 3 months of GA.
- Increase conversion from self-serve to enterprise by 20% by improving Dedicated contract discoverability and packaging.
- SLOs: 99.9% request success rate for Hosted; median generation latency < 120ms for 32-token responses on p4-class instance profiles (region-dependent).

Audience
--------
Primary: Product and engineering teams evaluating Redwood to run LLM features in production (hosted, dedicated, private). Secondary: Platform engineers responsible for procurement and operations.

Context and scope
-----------------
v9 focuses on these areas: Unified routing policies, rollout UX, cost and performance controls (bundled from Redwood Optimize), Dedicated packaging and committed capacity improvements, and Private deployment onboarding simplifications (VPC and on-prem templates). This doc covers product requirements, high-level design, roadmap, pricing guidance, and release notes for the v9 launch.

Core product pillars (v9)
-------------------------
1) Unified Routing & Fallbacks
   - Policy primitives: latency_target_ms, cost_target_cents_per_1k_tokens, region_preferences, allowed_models, fallback_order.
   - Automatic fallback to lower-cost quantized variants when cost_target exceeded or capacity constrained.

2) Rollouts & Safety
   - Canary/A-B infrastructures with traffic percentage controls, health checks (latency/error-rate), and automatic rollback on regression.

3) Cost Controls (bundled Optimize features)
   - Default batching profiles by route; prefix/KV caching per org; model/quantization recommendations surfaced in console.

4) Dedicated & Private UX Improvements
   - Dedicated: month-to-month reserved plans, flexible burst capacity.
   - Private: simplified VPC onboarding templates, automated KMS wiring for common clouds.

PRD: Requirements (priority and acceptance)
-----------------------------------------
The table below lists the product requirements for v9.

| ID | Requirement (user story) | Priority | Owner | Acceptance criteria |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| PRD-101 | As an app engineer, I can set routing policies that trade off cost and latency at per-route granularity. | P0 | Product + Eng-Serving | Console + API to set policy, policy enforced in runtime, documented examples. End-to-end test showing fallback to cheaper variant within 200ms of decision. |
| PRD-102 | As a platform engineer, I can create a Dedicated reservation with predictable throughput and optional burst. | P0 | Product + Eng-Infra | UI + API for reservation creation, capacity simulation tool, SLA page generated, e2e smoke test for throughput. |
| PRD-103 | As an SRE, I can configure canary rollouts with automatic rollback on 5% error-rate regression. | P1 | Eng-SRE | Canary config UI, rollback trigger implemented, post-deployment guardrail. |
| PRD-104 | As a customer admin, I can onboard Private deployments using cloud templates and automated KMS setup. | P1 | Eng-Private-Deployments | Template-driven onboarding with < 4 manual steps; KMS test key provisioning verified. |
| PRD-105 | As a developer, I see cost/latency recommendations in the Console and can apply them with one click. | P1 | Product + Eng-Platform | Recommendation panel with estimated savings; applying a recommendation updates routing config and shows simulation. |

Design specs (high level)
-------------------------
1. Policy model
   - Policy stored as a JSON blob with a small typed schema (fields: kind, latency_target_ms, cost_target_per_1k, allowed_models, fallbacks, regions, priority).
   - Runtime interprets policy and computes a routing score combining latency headroom, cost delta, and regional preference.

2. Runtime behavior
   - Decision window: routing decision must be computed within 10ms for cached model metadata; fallback enacted within first token generation when necessary.
   - Batching: per-route batching hints provided to runtime; continuous batching remains enabled with max_batch_size per instance.

3. Console UX
   - Unified routing page with a policy editor and per-route simulation panel.
   - Rollout UI: percentage slider, health metrics preview, and automatic rollback toggle.

4. Monitoring & Observability
   - New metrics: routing.decisions.total, routing.fallbacks.count, routing.latency.vs_target, rollout.automatic_rollbacks.count.
   - Traces: add routing policy id and evaluated score to request trace span.

Non-functional requirements
---------------------------
- Security: Policies are namespaced per-account and versioned; policy changes require audit log entry.
- Performance: Routing overhead adds < 2% p99 latency.
- Reliability: Fallback logic must be deterministic and testable in chaos runs.

Roadmap & release themes (quarterly view)
-----------------------------------------
- Q1 2026 (landed): Beta of unified routing + basic rollout primitives; initial Dedicated UI improvements.
- Q2 2026 (iter): Integrate Optimize cost recommendations; dedicated month-to-month reservations pilot.
- Q3 2026 (stabilize): Private onboarding templates, improved canary auto-rollback policies, SRE-run game days.
- Q4 2026 (v9 GA - target 2026-12-01): Full console polish, pricing & packaging updates, enterprise sales enablement materials, GA docs and release notes.

OKRs for launch
---------------
- O: Achieve 20% increase in paid Dedicated commitments within 6 months.
  - KR1: Increase Dedicated contract starts by 20% from baseline.
  - KR2: Reduce time-to-first-successful-dedicated-deployment to < 3 days.
- O: Improve unit economics for typical chat workloads by 15%.
  - KR1: Default batching/profile adoption rate > 60% on new orgs.

Pricing and packaging notes
--------------------------
High-level packaging
- Self-serve Hosted API: usage-based pricing retained (per-token + per-embedding). Default routing policies are applied, with 'Standard' Optimize settings.
- Dedicated: New tiering model - Reserved (12/6/1 month) + Burst plan.
- Private: Platform fee + node licensing; includes onboarding credits for first-month Professional Support.

Example pricing table (illustrative)
| Tier | Commitment | Effective list price (tokens) | Key characteristics |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Hosted Standard | none | $0.007 / 1k tokens | Self-serve, default routing, standard SLAs |
| Dedicated Reserved - Annual | 1 year | $0.0045 / 1k tokens (committed) | Predictable throughput, lower unit cost, SLA-backed |
| Dedicated Short - 1 month | 1 month | $0.0055 / 1k tokens | Fast onboarding, flexible cancellation, no long-term discount |
| Private (On-prem) | contract | Custom | Includes on-prem packaging and support |

Discounting guidance
- Standard discounts apply for > $100k ARR committed bookings. For Dedicated, offer volume-based sliding discounts at negotiation.
- Bundles: Redwood Optimize credits (cost-analysis reports, 90-day eval) offered as an add-on.

Sales enablement requirements
- New pitch deck describing Dedicated month-to-month and Reserved tiers.
- Pricing calculator spreadsheet that models committed vs burst economics for customer workloads.

Migration & upgrade notes
------------------------
- Existing customers on older routing models will be migrated: migration runs in two phases - 1) Read-only export of existing configurations; 2) Guided migration wizard in console that suggests default policy translations.
- Backwards compatibility guarantee: old policy blobs remain interpretable for 12 months.

Release notes (v9.0.0) - 2026-12-01
--------------------------------
Highlights
- GA: Unified routing policies with cost/latency primitives and automatic fallback to quantized variants.
- GA: Canary rollouts with automatic rollback on configurable health regressions.
- GA: Console recommendation panel (Optimize) with one-click apply.
- Dedicated: Month-to-month reservations and burst capacity UI.
- Private: New cloud onboarding templates and automated KMS wiring.

Notable bug fixes
- Fixed an edge case where batch scheduling could increase tail latency for short responses (PR#8421).
- Resolved false-positive rollback triggers in canary runs when synthetic traffic is sparse (PR#8562).

Migration steps for customers
1. Read the Migration Guide /confluence/product-docs/migration-to-unified-routing-v9.
2. Export current routing config (Admin > Routing > Export).
3. Run the Console migration wizard in a staging org; validate with the route simulator.
4. Rollout to production using a Canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with auto-rollback enabled.

Open risks and mitigations
-------------------------
- Risk: Customers may find policy DSL complex. Mitigation: provide templates and one-click recommendations, expand docs and examples.
- Risk: Incorrect fallback selection could reduce output quality. Mitigation: safety checks in runtime, quality regression tests, and customer-visible simulation prior to apply.

Appendix: Example policy JSON (illustrative)

  "kind": "latency-and-cost",

  "fallback_order": ["redwood-2-q4", "redwood-2-8bit"]
}

---------------------

- Engineering to publish migration automation and test harness by 2026-11-15.
